newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: FORECAST-Slovak c.bank sees SKK 52bln 96 trade gap.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Slovak c.bank sees SKK 52bln 96 trade gap.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Monday said it expects the 1996 trade deficit to reach about 52 billion crowns, near the top of its forecast range.
Elena Kohutikova, head of the NBS monetary policy department told a seminar on an OECD survey on Slovakia that the current account deficit should total some 45 billion crowns.
"We forecast the foreign trade deficit at some 52 billion crowns ($1.7 billion) and a current account deficit of some 45 billion crowns ($1.5 billion)," she said.
The NBS had previously said its estimate for the trade gap was between 50 and 52 billion crowns.
Slovakia's trade gap widened to 37.17 billion crowns for January-September from 35.078 billion in January-August.
"The increase in the foreign trade deficit at the end of the year does not worry us unduly, because this is traditional with an increase in imports for the holiday season," she added.

The NBS did not expect any problems in financing the current account deficit, Kohutikova said. This should be covered by the capital account surplus, which was $1.11 billion in the first eight months of this year.
The latest official figures show the current account deficit rose to $957.3 million for January-August from $847.2 million for the first seven months.
But Kohutikova noted that long-term investments, the most favourable foreign investment in Slovakia, were not developing in line with the needs of the current account.
At end-September foreign investment since the start of 1990 totalled $845 million.
